note: Seeds are placed in the soil to establish the winter crop ahead of the growing season.
Moisture triggers the seed to awaken and begin root and shoot development.
Young shoots break through the soil surface to establish plant population density.
The growing point transitions from vegetative growth to reproductive spike development.
The total number of potential spikelets and yield capacity begin to take shape.
The final leaf emerges, acting as the primary solar panel to power grain filling.
The wheat head emerges from the sheath as the crop nears flowering.
Critical stage where stress from drought and heat severely impacts final grain number.
Starch and proteins accumulate in the kernels, driving total yield and grain size.
Kernels reach maturity and dry down as the crop finishes active growth.
Grain moisture drops to harvest levels, signalling that the crop is ready to be combined.
